Name: Feature Store
Use Case: Reuse feature definitions for historical training retrieval and online inference
Strengths: Point-in-time historical joins; feature reuse; can reduce training-serving skew
Weaknesses: Timestamp correctness and materialization freshness require operational controls; backend capabilities vary
Alternatives: Feast; Tecton; Hopsworks; Vertex AI Feature Store; SageMaker Feature Store
Gotcha: Event-time joins alone can include later backfills; verify availability timestamps and backend support before assuming historical features match what serving knew

Name: Model Registry
Use Case: Version models and associate lifecycle metadata with their producing runs
Strengths: Versioned model references; run lineage; aliases and validation tags
Weaknesses: Approval enforcement and access controls depend on integration; registry metadata does not implement traffic splitting
Alternatives: MLflow Model Registry; Vertex AI Model Registry; SageMaker Model Registry
Gotcha: Aliases are mutable references; record the resolved model version for each deployment and implement rollout and rollback in the serving workflow

Name: Experiment Tracking
Use Case: Record experiment parameters and metrics with model artifacts and dataset references
Strengths: Run comparison; searchable metadata; links between datasets and model metrics
Weaknesses: Artifact retention costs; incomplete logging limits reproducibility; autologging support varies by framework
Alternatives: MLflow Tracking; Weights & Biases; Comet; ClearML
Gotcha: Log code revision and immutable data references with the execution environment; dataset metadata and metrics alone do not preserve all inputs needed to rerun training

Name: Online vs Offline Serving
Use Case: Choose synchronous request-time predictions or asynchronous batch scoring
Strengths: Online supports interactive requests; batch processes accumulated data without an immediate response requirement
Weaknesses: Online requires serving capacity; batch completion time and prediction freshness must fit the application
Alternatives: Managed online endpoints; Triton; KServe; vLLM; managed batch prediction jobs
Gotcha: Google Cloud online prediction requires endpoint deployment while batch jobs do not; measure end-to-end latency including feature retrieval rather than only model execution

Name: Training-Serving Skew
Use Case: Detect differences between training and serving data or preprocessing
Strengths: Shared transformation code reduces mismatch; sampled serving features support parity checks
Weaknesses: Changing joined data and feedback loops can persist despite shared infrastructure; production sampling needs privacy controls
Alternatives: Feature Store; shared preprocessing; TensorFlow Data Validation
Gotcha: Feature stores do not eliminate every source of skew; compare the same examples through training and serving paths and test on later data

Name: ML Pipeline Orchestration
Use Case: Coordinate data preparation and training with evaluation and deployment tasks
Strengths: Explicit task inputs and outputs; reusable components; caching avoids redundant executions
Weaknesses: Distributed debugging and artifact retention need ownership; caching can hide changes outside declared inputs
Alternatives: Kubeflow Pipelines; managed ML pipelines; Airflow; Dagster; Prefect
Gotcha: KFP can reuse outputs for identical inputs and parameters; pass immutable data versions and disable caching for mutable external reads or side-effecting deployment tasks

Name: Data Validation
Use Case: Check schemas and feature distributions before training and against serving data
Strengths: Detects missing or out-of-domain features; configurable skew and drift comparators; per-slice statistics
Weaknesses: Inferred schemas require domain review; thresholds and comparison metrics need calibration
Alternatives: TensorFlow Data Validation; Great Expectations; Pandera; Deequ
Gotcha: Model training-only labels explicitly with schema environments; passing schema checks does not establish model quality or absence of leakage

Name: Model Monitoring
Use Case: Compare production feature and prediction distributions and track labeled model quality when available
Strengths: Reference-versus-current drift checks; configurable thresholds; signals for investigation
Weaknesses: Drift is not proof of accuracy loss; delayed labels limit direct quality measurement; baseline selection affects alerts
Gotcha: Monitor missing values separately because drift tests may filter them out; investigate drift before retraining and evaluate replacement models before promotion

Name: GPU Resource Management
Use Case: Allocate dedicated or shared GPUs according to workload capacity and isolation requirements
Strengths: MIG provides hardware memory and fault isolation on supported GPUs; time-slicing enables oversubscription
Weaknesses: Time-slicing lacks memory and fault isolation between replicas; contention affects latency; MIG profiles and support vary
Alternatives: Dedicated GPUs; NVIDIA MIG; NVIDIA Kubernetes Device Plugin time-slicing
Gotcha: Time-sliced replicas are not isolated GPUs and requesting more replicas does not guarantee proportional compute; benchmark colocated workloads instead of assuming utilization gains

Name: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
Use Case: Supply retrieved external context to an LLM at query time
Strengths: Updates knowledge through retrieval without retraining model weights; supports fixed or agent-directed retrieval flows
Weaknesses: Retrieval and generation can both fail; source freshness and context limits matter; iterative retrieval adds variable latency
Alternatives: LangChain; LlamaIndex; Haystack; custom retrieval + LLM
Gotcha: Evaluate retrieval relevance and answer correctness separately; tune chunking on representative questions rather than assuming a universal size or that citations prove correctness

Name: Vector Database
Use Case: Store embeddings and retrieve neighbors using a chosen distance metric
Strengths: Exact search is available in systems such as pgvector; approximate indexes offer tunable recall and speed
Weaknesses: Index memory and build costs; filtered ANN can return too few matches; latency depends on workload
Alternatives: Pinecone; Weaviate; Qdrant; Milvus; Chroma; pgvector
Gotcha: Measure ANN recall against exact search under real filters; pgvector uses hnsw.ef_search or ivfflat.probes and supports bounded iterative scans for filtered queries

Name: LLM Fine-Tuning
Use Case: Adapt pretrained models using full weight updates or parameter-efficient adapters
Strengths: LoRA trains low-rank updates while freezing base weights; compact adapters can reduce training memory and storage
Weaknesses: Benefits depend on rank and target modules; base model resources remain necessary; task quality needs held-out evaluation
Alternatives: Full fine-tuning; LoRA; QLoRA; prefix tuning; prompting or RAG without weight updates
Gotcha: LoRA has no universal parameter reduction or quality guarantee; record the base model revision and adapter configuration and evaluate before merging or deploying

Name: LLM and RAG Evaluation
Use Case: Compare application versions before release and monitor sampled production behavior
Strengths: Versioned evaluation datasets; component-level scoring; complementary human and automated review
Weaknesses: LLM judges require calibration; curated sets can miss production cases; evaluation adds inference and review cost
Alternatives: LangSmith; deterministic evaluators; human annotation workflows
Gotcha: Separate answer correctness from groundedness and retrieval relevance; pin dataset and judge configurations and review judge agreement with humans before using scores as release gates

Name: LLM Guardrails and Tool Approval
Use Case: Apply checks to model inputs and outputs and require approval for sensitive tool actions
Strengths: PII handling; deterministic and model-based checks; human approval before configured tool execution
Weaknesses: Rules miss nuanced violations; model checks add cost and latency; guardrails do not guarantee safety or compliance
Alternatives: LangChain middleware; application policy checks; human approval workflows
Gotcha: Input-only PII filtering does not cover outputs or tool results; configure each boundary explicitly and keep authorization separate from model-based safety judgments

Name: Training Reproducibility and Determinism
Use Case: Control randomness and execution conditions to make training comparisons and regressions interpretable
Strengths: Seeded generators and data-loader workers; deterministic algorithm selection; repeatable debugging within a controlled environment
Weaknesses: Deterministic operations may be slower or unavailable; identical seeds do not guarantee results across releases or devices
Alternatives: PyTorch deterministic algorithms; seeded data loaders; pinned execution environments
Gotcha: Record code and data versions plus framework and hardware settings; seed every relevant RNG and do not promise bitwise equivalence across CPU and GPU or framework upgrades
